text: Use rmcp crate for MCP protocol over stdio
reason: Purpose-built for MCP stdio transport; avoids hand-rolling JSON-RPC protocol handling
impact: Determines server scaffolding, tool registration pattern, and protocol compatibility surface

text: Use std::fs::canonicalize for symlink resolution and path normalization
reason: Built-in, well-tested, handles .. and symlinks in one system call
alternatives: manual path normalization with symlink checking
impact: Core security boundary — all path validation depends on this behavior

text: Resolve all roots to canonical form at startup
reason: Catches misconfigured roots early; ensures consistent comparison throughout server lifetime
impact: Startup validation catches config errors before any tool is invoked

text: Most-specific-root-wins for overlapping roots (sort by path depth descending)
reason: Deterministic, intuitive; deeper path = more specific grant; enables broad read-only with narrow read-write carve-outs
impact: Users can grant broad read-only access with targeted read-write directories underneath

text: Relative paths allowed only with exactly one root; rejected with multiple roots
reason: Avoids ambiguity; simple to explain and implement; single-root is the common case
impact: Simple UX for single-root users; multi-root users use absolute paths

text: edit_file defaults to dryRun:true when client omits the flag
reason: Prevents accidental destructive edits; AI coding agents often preview before applying
impact: Safety-first default; spec section 10.6 recommends this behavior

text: Do not follow symlinked directories in directory_tree and search_files by default
reason: Prevents infinite loops and accidental traversal outside the logical tree
impact: Safe default; configurable via followSymlinkedDirectories flag

text: Use similar crate for unified diff generation in edit_file
reason: Pure Rust, no system dependency on diff binary, consistent output across platforms
impact: Portable diff output; no external binary dependency

text: Use walkdir + ignore crates for search_files and directory_tree
reason: walkdir handles recursive filesystem traversal; ignore adds gitignore-style exclude pattern support
impact: Both crates are well-tested; the combination handles ignore files and glob patterns naturally

text: Limit configuration format to JSON only
reason: One format reduces maintenance; JSON is universal in the MCP ecosystem; users editing MCP config already work in JSON
impact: Simpler code, fewer dependencies, consistent with MCP client config format

text: Use Tokio for async runtime with spawn_blocking for filesystem operations
reason: MCP transport is async; filesystem operations are blocking; Tokio is the Rust async standard
impact: Largest ecosystem, best MCP crate compatibility, widespread community knowledge
